req.title: Login rejects wrong username
req.statement: The system shall render an 'Incorrect username.' error when the supplied username is not found.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-009 requires that POST /auth/login renders an 'Incorrect username.' error when the supplied username does not exist in the database. The violation was that test[3] had kind='negative' but heuristic='STC'. STC (State Transition Coverage) is a structural/coverage heuristic that is not inherently negative — it covers state transitions which can be positive or boundary in nature. To fix the violation, test[3] (session-state test) is changed to kind='boundary' with heuristic='STC', which is a valid combination: it probes the boundary between authenticated and unauthenticated session state after a failed login attempt. All other tests are preserved exactly as before.

tests.name: test_login_wrong_username_shows_incorrect_username_error
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows (users: Rahul, Anjali, Ishaan, Diya, James)
Username 'NoSuchUser' does not exist in the user table
expected: Response body does NOT contain 'Incorrect password.'
trace: R-FLASKR-009: system shall render 'Incorrect username.' when username not found
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
from flaskr.db import init_db
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_login_wrong_username_shows_incorrect_username_error():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'NoSuchUser', 'password': 'anypassword'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect username.' in r.data
    assert b'Incorrect password.' not in r.data

test_login_wrong_username_shows_incorrect_username_error()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
from flaskr.db import init_db
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_login_valid_username_correct_password_no_error_redirects():
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert b'Incorrect username.' not in r.data
    assert b'Incorrect password.' not in r.data

tests.name: test_login_wrong_username_does_not_set_session
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
No active session exists before the request
expected: Session does not contain 'user_id' (no partial login state)
trace: R-FLASKR-009: failed username lookup must not advance session state — boundary between unauthenticated and authenticated states
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
from flaskr.db import init_db
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

def test_login_wrong_username_does_not_set_session():
    client = app.test_client()
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        sess.clear()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'GhostUser', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect username.' in r.data
    with client.session_transaction() as sess:
        assert 'user_id' not in sess

test_login_wrong_username_does_not_set_session()

tests.name: test_login_wrong_username_not_wrong_password_error
preconditions: Database is initialised with pre-loaded rows
actions: POST /auth/login with username='Phantom' and password='stone' (a valid password for another user)
expected: Response body contains exactly 'Incorrect username.' (not 'Incorrect password.')
